questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number.

4 : 80 : 5 : ?
questions.solution:
The logic is:

4 : 80 → 4 : 4² × (4 + 1)

Similarly,

5 : ? → 5 : 5² × (5 + 1)

⇒ ? = 25 × 6

⇒ ? = 150

Hence, ‘150’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: In a certain code language if ‘TRANSIT’ is coded as ‘202’. How will ‘ROUTINE’ be coded in the same language?
questions.solution:
The logic is: Add all the place value and multiply by 2 to get the code

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b06c01734f8aa4c011a0a36a57e3bea6aebf56189f0aedd590f9d0d65a852ad3.png] 

TRANSIT = (20 + 18 + 1 + 14 + 19 + 9 + 20) × 2 = 202

Similarly,

ROUTINE = (18 + 15 + 21 + 20 + 9 + 14 + 5) × 2 = 204

Hence, ‘204’ is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Two statements and three conclusions I, II and III are given below. Assuming the statements to be true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some gifts are jwelleries.

All the jwelleries are designs.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some designs are gifts.

II. Some jwelleries are gifts.

III. None of the designs are gifts.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.
Either conclusion I or III follows.
Only conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c581783eabc443ff3881e12f7a4a5dabfc88994b9af71911ea19ebcc47fb466.png] 

I. Some designs are gifts. → True (As, Some gifts are jewelleries and All the jewelleries are designs.)

II. Some jewelleries are gifts. → True (As, Some gifts are jewelleries)

III. None of the designs are gifts. → False (Some gifts are jewelleries and All the jewelleries are designs. So, some designs are gifts)

Hence, only conclusions I and II follow.

questions.question:
There are two statements and four conclusions I, II, III and IV are given below. Assuming the statements to be true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All the trains are scooters.

All the buses are scooters.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some scooters are train.

II. No train is a bus.

III. Some trains are buses.

IV. No scooter is a train.

options.text: Conclusion I and either conclusion III or IV follow.
Conclusion I and either conclusion II or III follow.
Only conclusions I and III follow.
Only conclusions I and IV follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7828457a2d0075cdfcc20c679a14187a0faf339f96fa26a29b281172cebf00da.png] 

I. Some scooters are train. → True (As, All the trains are scooters.)

II. No train is a bus. → False (It can be possible, but it is not definite)

III. Some trains are buses. → False (It can be possible, but it is not definite)

IV. No scooter is a train. → False (As, All the trains are scooters.)

Conclusion II and III forms a complementary pair.

Hence, conclusion I and either conclusion II or III follow.
